translations.en: Insect damage means we can't tell which floor it was on,
but we have two clues: Leiden Street and a broken statue.
translations.note: Both Leiden Street and the broken statue are required clues; insect damage hides the floor number.

translations.en: I think it'll be quite a difficult search,
but I want you to protect me and take me there.
No, then...
I thought you might say that.
You can't trust me.
Even I wouldn't accept a request from me.
But there really might be a weapon that can defeat our enemy!
Can't you please reconsider?
I'd appreciate it if you'd think of this as one last chance for me.
I don't want to be a coward
who thinks of nothing but running away!
So if you decide to give me another chance,
come and talk to me anytime.
Um... There's something I'd really like to ask you.
I've been researching @7rChu Lu Gah@0r,
and I found some information that caught my attention.
I'd like you to come with me to investigate it.
I'm not trying to run away again.
After everything I've done, you might not believe me,
but this time I really was researching for the people of this city.
It isn't information about escaping.
We might actually be able to fight the sealed monster.
That's what I want to investigate. Will you come with me?
@7rCyrus@0r usually avoids your gaze,
but today he looks you straight in the eye
as he makes his request. What should you do?
You received a @3rCrimson Dress@0r.
Let's drink right away! Cheers!
Gulp, gulp, gulp...
Deeeelicious!
Three hundred years
can make a drink taste this good?!
I wondered what all the fuss was about. Three-hundred-year-old liquor?
You did well to realize it had to be in a glass bottle.
Why a glass bottle?
Barrels give liquor color and flavor.
But what do you think happens if it gets too much of those?
What do you mean?
What happens if you keep pouring salt into a stew?
Say, three hundred grams, or even three kilograms?
It gets so salty you can't eat it.
Oh, I see what you mean.
After aging it in a barrel for the right amount of time,
you let it mature quietly in a glass or ceramic bottle.
I see!
Oh, right. I haven't paid you yet.
Thanks for the delicious liquor!
From @7rFiore@0r, you received a reward of @3r100,000 G@0r.
And you can have this too!
From @7rFiore@0r, you received a @3rCrimson Dress@0r.
Tonight, we're drinking till dawn!
You received @3rWork Clothes@0r.
Gaaaaaaaaah!
What?! What on earth is wrong?
Th-the three-hundred-year-old liquor from the barrel...
Tastes HOOOOORRIBLE!
A barrel? Of course it does!
Tannins and things have seeped out of the wood.
That isn't liquor anymore!
Whaaaat?! Really?!
You fool. It depends on the drink, but liquor can only age in a barrel
for twenty to sixty years at most. After that,
it has to be stored in glass or ceramic bottles.
Bleeeeeurgh.
So that's why it was such a thick, weird liquid that reeked of wood.
Oh... So this is what a wasted effort feels like...
And paying your reward is going to leave my purse empty...
@7rFiore@0r reluctantly hands you your @3r50,000 G@0r reward.
That's a pretty meager reward, isn't it...?
You've been through a lot, so I'll give you this item too!
From @7rFiore@0r, you received @3rWork Clothes@0r.
Oh, to hell with it! I'm drowning my sorrows tonight!
Come on, let's get going!
Liquor like you've never seen before is waiting for us!
Have you changed your mind?
It'd really help me if you have.
What do you say? Will you help me out?
I'll pay you properly!

context: Cyrus seeks redemption through the grave investigation; Fiore's liquor quest branches into bottled success or spoiled barrel contents.
decisions: Control tokens remain on their source rows and in their original sequence. Genuine sentence continuations retain row boundaries; other omitted subjects are restored from scene context. Unknown historical warrior gender stays neutral. Item names follow the shared glossary; established imported prose and provenance remain intact.
